NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday countered Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for pinning the blame for Gulzar Singh's suicide on Aam Aadmi Party-led Punjab government, advising him not to "do politics over dead bodies."In a social media post on X, Mann said that all the accused have been caught by the police based on identification by the family."Rahul Gandhi ji, don't do politics over dead bodies; Punjabis don't like this kind of politics," Mann said.Mann also shared a video in which a Congress leader was seen facing villagers' protest."Look here, when Congress leaders went to the victim's village and still tried to indulge in this dirty politics, the people chased them away from there," the chief minister said."In this case, all the accused have already been caught by the police based on identification by the family. The Akali, BJP, and Congress governments have been responsible for spreading drugs in Punjab. In my government, no drug smuggler will be spared," Mann said.Earlier in the day, Rahul accused the AAP of "crushing those who question" the Punjab government after Gulzar - a villager in Punjab - died by suicide following alleged pressure to apologise for publicly questioning the state's finance minister over the drug menace in the state.In a social media post on X, Rahul said Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should immediately demand his minister Harpal Singh Cheema's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation."A dangerous pattern is emerging in Punjab's AAP government - if you question government failures, the response will come in the form of threats and torture," Rahul said."Gulzar Singh ji, from the Dalit community, who had to watch his son fall victim to drugs, asked the finance minister just this much: why has the government failed so miserably in stopping the drug trade? For just this, he was tortured and humiliated so much, pressured so intensely to apologise, that he consumed poison. Wandering from one hospital to another, without access to treatment, he ultimately lost the battle for his life," he added.He said the government's job is to answer to the people, "not to crush those who ask questions"."The government's job is to answer to the people, not to crush those who ask questions. May Gulzar Singh ji's family get justice as soon as possible. The chief minister should immediately demand the finance minister's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation, with his name registered in the FIR," the Congress leader said.A controversy erupted after a 47-year-old man, Gulzar Singh, from Sangrur allegedly died by suicide, with his family claiming that he was asked to apologise and subjected to casteist slurs for questioning finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the "unabated" supply of 'chitta' in his area at an event on September 6.Singh died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison, his family members said.A purported video of Gulzar's last moments surfaced in which he spoke about questioning the finance minister, prompting opposition parties to demand the resignations of Cheema as well as Mann.Punjab Police set up a special investigation team (SIT), led by an officer of additional director general of police rank, in connection with the suicide incident.Following a complaint by Gulzar's family, five villagers - Baljit Singh, Sukhdev Singh, Vicky Singh, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur - have been booked under Section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and relevant sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, according to the FIR.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accused the AAP of "crushing those who question" the Punjab government. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann said that all the accused have been caught by the police based on identification by the family. A controversy erupted after a 47-year-old man, Gulzar Singh, from Sangrur, allegedly died by suicide.

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday condemned strikes by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabian oil and civilian facilities, saying that such attacks undermine regional security."India condemns attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, especially the targeting of civilian and economic facilities. Attacks that undermine regional security and stability and threaten freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb were unacceptable," ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to a media query.Jaiswal’s remarks came as the Houthis, the Yemen-based rebel group, targeted Saudi oil facilities and other civilian infrastructure on Tuesday, raising widespread concerns over a further escalation of the conflict in the Middle East.The attacks on Saudi Arabia came as the US intensified its economic sanctions against Iran.As many as 73 people were wounded in a wave of Houthi attacks that targeted “civilian and economic facilities” in the Saudi Arabian cities of Abha, Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait.The strikes came hours after the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out an air strike on a prison in Yemen’s northern Jawf province. At least seven people, including a child, were killed and seven others wounded in the strike in the city of Hazem.Yemen’s civil war began in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, along with large parts of northern Yemen, forcing the internationally recognised government into exile.A Saudi-led coalition, which included the United Arab Emirates, intervened the following year in an effort to restore the government to power.Tensions between the US allies Saudi Arabia and the UAE escalated earlier this year as their partnership in Yemen’s war deteriorated, ultimately prompting the UAE to withdraw from the conflict.The civil war has killed at least 150,000 people, according to UN estimates, and at times pushed Yemen to the brink of famine.
Article Summary: India condemns attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, especially the targeting of civilian and economic facilities. Attacks that undermine regional security and stability and threaten freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb were unacceptable. strikes came hours after the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out an air strike on a prison in Yemen's northern Jawf province.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday took cognisance of Greater Noida executive magistrate's notice to a 2nd year law student for participating in a protest led by Cockroach Janata Party.Though the notice was withdrawn, the apex court said that it is a serious matter as its September 1 pan-India direction barred action against students.According to the Live Law, the matter was brought to the attention of a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant."How could a magistrate dare to issue notice? We made clear no coercive action against any student! No magistrate could violate that order," CJI said.This comes a day after Allahabad high court reprimanded Noida DM Medha Roopam for imposing the National Security Act on Delhi University student activist Akriti Chaudhary, saying that errant bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian dystopia" and reminded civil servants that their loyalty lies with the Constitution and not the political executive.A division bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev observed that bureaucrats and police officers enjoy immense powers because they are entrusted with protecting the constitutional rights, dignity and welfare of citizens."They must remember that their loyalty is towards the Constitution and not the political executive," the court said.The 15-page order, made public days after the court quashed the NSA detention and awarded Rs 5 lakh compensation to Chaudhary on Sept 2, contains sharp criticism of the Gautam Budh Nagar administration and police for invoking the stringent preventive detention law against a student activist without adequate material.Warning against abuse of authority, the bench observed that when officials disregard their constitutional oath, they risk being perceived as "an oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating conditions for civil unrest. "It shall not be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia," the court remarked.The bench was particularly critical of Gautam Budh Nagar DM Medha Roopam, who had approved the NSA detention.It held that where the police dossier contained only allegations and no credible supporting material, the district magistrate was expected to scrutinise the records threadbare before invoking the extraordinary powers available under the NSA.Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April 2026. The UP Police invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among activists arrested in cases related to the protest seeking higher wages.
Article Summary: Supreme Court took cognisance of Greater Noida executive magistrate's notice to a 2nd year law student for participating in a protest led by Cockroach Janata Party. This comes a day after Allahabad high court reprimanded Noida DM Medha Roopam for imposing National Security Act on Delhi University student activist Akriti Chaudhary.

NEW DELHI: Amruta Fadnavis , wife of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , said there was nothing wrong with Muslims participating in Navratri and other festivals, after the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) called for Muslims to be barred from the upcoming Navratri festivities, a demand endorsed by state minister Nitesh Rane.“Festivals are inclusive, and there is nothing wrong with a Muslim person attending the celebrations. NEW DELHI: The Congress ' West Bengal unit on Tuesday lodged a police complaint against Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri over his recent “avoid non-veg during Durga Puja” remark, asserting that the call was “intended to create disharmony. ”In the complaint submitted to the officer-in-charge of Kolkata’s Bhawanipore police station, the South Kolkata District Congress Committee alleged that Shastri made “derogatory” comments during an event in Howrah on September 5.“We want to apprise you that immediate administrative action needs to be initiated, and an FIR needs to be registered with necessary arrests. His remarks could spark disharmony in society and were against the democratic spirit,” Congress leader Pradip Prasad said in the complaint, according to PTI.The self-styled godman, popularly known as “Bageshwar Baba," had appealed to Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food during the Durga Puja festivities and described those who eat meat on religious occasions as “hypocrites."The Congress’ move put it on the same page as the BJP, West Bengal’s ruling party, in a rare display of unity between the two national rivals.BJP West Bengal chief Samik Bhattacharya had already rejected Shastri’s call, saying that Bengalis would “continue to eat what they have been eating.”“We generally eat ‘luchi’ on Ashtami and goat meat on Navami. We will continue to do that. Nobody can tell the people of West Bengal what they should eat,” Bhattacharya said.“Let me live the way I want to. Bengalis will eat what they have been eating. Can Bengalis not eat fish and meat?” he asked, quoting Swami Vivekananda.While saying that he respected Shastri as a religious figure, Bhattacharya argued that the self-styled godman’s personal views should not dictate what Bengali society should eat.The issue has sparked a wider debate in West Bengal, where fish and meat are closely associated with traditional Bengali cuisine, while religious practices vary across communities and regions.Durga Puja, celebrated with great pomp and fervour in West Bengal, will be held from October 16-20.
Article Summary: Congress lodges police complaint against Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri. The self-styled godman had appealed to Bengalis to give up non- vegetarian food during the Durga Puja festivities. The Congress' move put it on the same page as the BJP, West Bengal’s ruling party.

Article Title: Eiffel Tower shuts after staff strike over BAPS visit
Article Text:

Eiffel Tower in Paris was closed to visitors Monday after staff suddenly went on strike, alleging that female employees were moved from their stations during a visit by a delegation from a Gujarat-based Hindu religious group.A 100-strong delegation linked to Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) had visited Eiffel Tower ahead of Festival of Cultures, marking the consecration of a Swaminarayan Temple in Paris over the weekend.PTI quoted workers' union representative Diane Davoine as saying women members of the staff were asked to leave their stations as the delegation arrived at the tourism landmark. Confederation Generale du Travail, a national forum of trade unions, alleged that in some cases, women employees were temporarily replaced by male colleagues and told to avoid particular areas till the religious delegation left.The operating company, Societe d'Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), said the tower reopened as usual on Tuesday, acknowledging that a BAPS delegation had requested "limited interactions with women" and that the condition "should not have been accepted".BAPS issued a detailed statement insisting the arrangements were never gender-based. It said the visit was coordinated in advance purely for logistical reasons."Given the size of the group, this visit was coordinated in advance with the Eiffel Tower's management team and was scheduled at the start of normal operating hours specifically to minimise any disruption to staff, other visitors, and the site's regular functioning." MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the matter was purely between the entities concerned.BAPS regretted any inconvenience caused to employees by the arrangements. "We take seriously the concerns expressed by the Eiffel Tower's employees, and we sincerely regret any inconvenience or discomfort caused to them as a result of the arrangements made for our group's visit."Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire called the employees' anger legitimate. National Assembly President Yael Braun-Pivet said women in France fully occupy public spaces and cannot be told to make themselves invisible. Gender equality minister Aurore Berge called the episode unacceptable, saying no religion is above the Republic's laws. Former PM Gabriel Attal backed Tower's staff, saying no culture or belief can dictate a woman's place.
Article Summary: Workers' union representative Diane Davoine said women members of the staff were asked to leave their stations as the delegation arrived at the tourism landmark. A 100-strong delegation linked to Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) had visited Eiffel Tower ahead of Festival of Cultures. BAPS issued a detailed statement insisting the arrangements were never gender-based.

Article Title: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta found hanging at Noida residence, dies by suicide
Article Text:
Rakesh Mehta Former Delhi Chief Secretary

NEW DELHI: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta , who served during chief minister Sheila Dikshit ’s tenure, allegedly died by suicide at his residence in Noida, officials said on Tuesday.Mehta, 74, a 1975-batch IAS officer, was found hanging from a ceiling fan at his Sector 82 residence on September 6, officials told news agency PTI.Noida Police recovered a purported suicide note in which he cited his "mental and health issues" as the reasons behind the extreme step.Mehta's body was cremated at the Lodhi Road crematorium on Monday.Mehta served as Delhi's chief secretary for more than three years, taking charge in 2007 and retiring in November 2010. The 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi were organised during his tenure.He was credited with overseeing the execution of several key transport, power and civic infrastructure projects in the national capital.Mehta held several positions in the Delhi government during his career and also served as commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, according to his former colleagues.(with inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Rakesh Mehta, 74, a 1975-batch IAS officer, was found hanging from a ceiling fan at his Sector 82 residence on September 6. Police recovered a purported suicide note in which he cited his "mental and health issues" as the reasons behind the extreme step. The 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi were organised during his tenure.

Article Title: 'You can't keep it lingering': Supreme Court to Odisha on Dara Singh plea
Article Text:
‘You can’t keep it lingering’: SC

NEW DELHI: Pulling up Odisha govt over its indecisiveness on taking a call on the remission plea of Dara Singh, SC Tuesday said the state cannot linger on the issue and made it clear that the official (secretary) concerned will be summoned if decision is not taken by Sept 17, the next date of hearing.A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi expressed displeasure after Odisha govt sought a four-week adjournment on the ground of illness of its advocate-on-record (AoR). Deferring the hearing, the court made it clear that no adjournment will be granted on the next date. "You cannot keep it lingering like this. Take a decision, accept or reject. You cannot avoid taking decision," the bench said.Noting that hearing in the case had been adjourned multiple times to allow the state to take a call on the remission plea, the court at the previous hearing also expressed displeasure over State Sentence Review Board not having made a decision yet. SC made it clear to state govt that it would have to pass an order if the authority did not make a decision.
Article Summary: Odisha govt sought a four-week adjournment on the ground of illness of its advocate-on-record. SC made it clear that the official (secretary) concerned will be summoned if decision is not taken by Sept 17. "You cannot keep it lingering like this. Take a decision, accept or reject," the bench said.

NEW DELHI: Confrontation hit Parliament Street police station Tuesday after a group of Congress SC/ST MPs petitioned police for an FIR for the “untouchability-purification” committed against party president Mallikarjun Kharge , but cops refused to file the case. After three hours of deadlock, police informed the delegation that Haldwani police has registered an FIR and provided a copy of it, after which the Congress delegation departed.The police complaint was submitted after MPs failed to get an invite from the President despite a request for a meeting.The 37-member delegation included MPs Kodikunnil Suresh, Karamvir Baudh, Sasikanth Senthil, Saptgiri Ulaka, Varsha Gaikwad, Gowaal Padavi, Christopher Tilak, Balram Naik, Vamsi Gaddam, Shyamkumar Barve, Saleng Sangma, and AICC Dalit department managers K Raju and Rajendra Pal Gautam.Signed by Congress MP Mallu Ravi, the complaint sought action against the identified persons in the Haldwani case while alleging BJP’s involvement in the act, which, it said, has hurt Dalits in the country and internationally. It said the “purification” of the rally venue after Kharge’s public meeting demonstrated practice of “untouchability” which is a violation of the Constitution, and a crime under the penal code, the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, and the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.“The acts of the accused are prejudicial to the unity and integrity of the country and promote social discrimination. Their criminal acts have spread the message in society that persons belonging to the SCs are considered inferior and impure, which is contrary to the spirit of abolition of untouchability enshrined in Article 17 of the Constitution,” the complaint said.

Article Title: Satya Niketan building collapse: MCD crackdown begins across Delhi; 24 properties demolished, 7 sealed
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has demolished 24 properties and sealed seven illegal structures across the capital following the building collapse in south Delhi’s Satya Niketan that killed seven people.According to the MCD data, quoted by news agency PTI, the civic body stepped up its enforcement drive against unauthorised construction, carrying out demolition action against 17 properties and sealing five on Tuesday alone. It also issued nine show-cause notices for unauthorised construction, two notices for sealing and 15 demolition orders, the report said.On Monday, the MCD had demolished seven properties, sealed two and issued 26 show-cause notices for unauthorised construction, four notices for sealing and 12 demolition orders.The action follows the collapse of a five-storey building in Satya Niketan on Sunday, which killed at least seven people and injured several others. The incident brought renewed scrutiny of unauthorised construction and civic enforcement in the capital.Additionally, the MCD on Monday suspended South Zone deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar and four engineers pending disciplinary proceedings.According to MCD officials, enforcement action has been carried out across all 12 zones, including Laxmi Nagar, Vishwas Nagar, Mukherjee Nagar, Jamia Nagar, Shaheen Bagh, Tilak Nagar, Karam Pura, Karol Bagh, Ramesh Nagar, Mansarovar Garden, Chandni Chowk and Nehru Vihar.Several of these areas have substantial student populations.The drive followed a meeting between Delhi lieutenant governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and senior government and MCD officials. Authorities were directed to conduct inspections in paying guest (PG) accommodation hubs, particularly buildings suspected of violating height and floor restrictions.Sandhu also directed the chief secretary to ensure structural audits of all buildings in PG hubs within a week.Between September 1 and 8, the MCD demolished 48 properties and sealed 15, besides issuing 90 show-cause notices for unauthorised construction, 124 notices for sealing and 66 demolition orders.From June 1 to September 8, the civic body demolished 1,007 properties and sealed 471 others. It also issued 1,551 show-cause notices for unauthorised construction, 714 notices for sealing and 753 demolition orders.
Article Summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has demolished 24 properties and sealed seven illegal structures. The action follows the collapse of a five-storey building in Satya Niketan on Sunday, which killed at least seven people and injured several others. The incident brought renewed scrutiny of unauthorised construction and civic enforcement in the capital.

Article Title: 'Releasing 6,000 cusecs is impossible': Karnataka on Cauvery water order, may move Supreme Court
Article Text:
File photo: A drone view of the dry riverbed as Cauvery water flow remains low at Mukkombu Dam, in Tiruchirappalli (Picture credit: ANI)

Karnataka may approach SC

NEW DELHI: The Karnataka government is seriously considering approaching the Supreme Court against the direction to release 6,000 cusecs of Cauvery river water daily to Tamil Nadu, state water resources minister N Chaluvarayaswamy said on Tuesday.The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) on Tuesday recommended that Karnataka ensure a flow of 6,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.The recommendation was subsequently upheld by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).Chaluvarayaswamy described the CWRC order as "absurd" and said Karnataka was facing a difficult situation because inflows into the Cauvery basin had declined significantly over the past week."Our officials strongly argued the ground realities at the CWRC meeting. Tamil Nadu had sought 17,000 cusecs of water. However, inflows into the Cauvery basin have declined considerably over the past week. In such a distress situation, even releasing 6,000 cusecs is impossible for us. We are making continuous efforts to ensure that no water is released," Chaluvarayaswamy told reporters.Also read: CWMA directs Karnataka to release 6,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu for 15 days Chaluvarayaswamy said the state government did not expect much relief from the CWMA meeting and would discuss the issue with chief minister D K Shivakumar before deciding on approaching the Supreme Court."...we will discuss the matter with the chief minister. The government is seriously considering filing a petition in the Supreme Court tomorrow itself," he said.The minister also criticised authorities taking decisions from Delhi, saying they did not understand the situation on the ground."The Constitution and administration benches sitting in Delhi do not understand the ground realities. There have been instances in the past when similar orders were issued without understanding the actual situation," he said.The CWMA on Tuesday upheld the CWRC recommendation directing Karnataka to ensure a flow of 6,000 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.The decision was taken at the 57th meeting of the CWMA in Delhi under the chairmanship of SK Haldar, with officials from Karnataka and Tamil Nadu participating.The latest direction followed the CWMA's August 25 order, when it upheld a CWRC recommendation directing Karnataka to ensure a flow of 9,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.The meeting came a day after the Supreme Court directed the Tamil Nadu government to raise its grievance over Karnataka's release of its proportionate share of Cauvery water before the CWMA.At its August 24 meeting, the CWRC had directed Karnataka to release water from its reservoirs and ensure a flow of 9,000 cusecs at the Biligundulu border point for 15 days. Tamil Nadu was expected to receive approximately 11.66 TMC of water during that period.The Karnataka minister said around 50% of the available water in the state's various reservoirs was being reserved exclusively for drinking water purposes."Water has been supplied to farmers' crops as required through the Bhadra and Upper Krishna Project (UKP) in those regions. Water has also been released through the river to ensure there is no drinking water shortage in the Chitradurga region," he said.He added that water from reservoirs was being managed in a controlled manner to fill lakes and ponds and prevent shortages for people and livestock.The latest order is part of a series of directions on Cauvery water releases. Earlier, the CWRC had directed Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12, with the CWMA subsequently upholding that decision.

Article Title: SC to consider Satya Niketan case transfer from Delhi HC over PG building collapse

Supreme Court weighs taking over proceedings

The Supreme Court on Tuesday said it would examine on September 10 whether the issues arising from the Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi should be taken up by the top court, potentially bringing the case under its ongoing pan-India proceedings.A bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan was hearing a plea seeking urgent intervention after the five-storey building housing a boys' paying guest accommodation collapsed near Delhi University 's South Campus on Sunday. Seven students were killed and five others were injured.The court noted that the Delhi high court was already dealing with the incident but said the issues raised appeared to overlap with a broader case before the Supreme Court concerning unauthorised construction, fire safety and illegal conversion of residential properties for commercial use."We have something in mind. We will consider this issue day-after-tomorrow. This is a serious issue. The issues dealt with by the high court are overlapping with one considered by this court on pan-India basis," the bench said.Senior advocate Ajit Sinha, who is serving as amicus curiae in the Supreme Court matter, told the bench that he had inspected the collapse site along with an IIT professor and MCD officials following the incident.He also placed a status report before the court and urged it to hear the matter urgently so that directions could be issued.The Supreme Court has previously issued several directions to authorities concerning unauthorised construction in residential areas, fire safety and the conversion of residential properties into commercial establishments in violation of rules.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Delhi government, informed the bench that the Delhi High Court was already hearing a PIL on the incident and placed its Monday order on record.He described the collapse as "most unfortunate" and said, "Our heart goes out to the children and the parents".The Delhi high court on Monday ordered a high-level inquiry by the MCD into the collapse and said the government could not escape responsibility.The court described the incident as "most unfortunate" and said such tragedies were linked to inadequate measures by the MCD and other authorities.The rescue operation at the site ended after more than 27 hours on Monday, with seven people dead and five injured. Police arrested the building owner, his wife and son, while five MCD officials were suspended.The building collapsed at around 1.30 pm on Sunday. Article Title: TN Assembly passes resolution urging Centre to use official OBC names in 2027 Census

Why Tamil Nadu wants fixed caste names

OBC caste data absent from post-Independence Census

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu Assembly on Tuesday unanimously passed a resolution asking the Centre to use only officially recognised caste names while collecting data on Other Backward Classes during the second phase of the 2027 Census.The resolution covers Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities listed by the Tamil Nadu and Union governments. It also calls for these official lists to be built into the census portal so that people can select their caste from a fixed list rather than enter names themselves.The resolution said caste details should be collected for these communities in the same manner as data for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.Minister for Backward Classes Welfare V Sampathkumar, who moved the resolution, said allowing people to enter different names for the same caste could create confusion, particularly when regional variations are involved.He said such ambiguity could make enumeration difficult and affect the usefulness of the census data."Hence, the exercise must stick to official names alone as per the notifications of the state and union governments to ensure social justice and equal justice," he said.The minister suggested that the official lists of BCs, MBCs and Denotified Communities should be pre-loaded into the census enumeration portal or application. Enumerators or respondents could then select the relevant caste using a 'drop-down menu'.The resolution also called for the 'open-column method' to be completely avoided while collecting details of these communities.The Assembly said caste-wise data on OBCs has not been included in censuses conducted after Independence. It argued that accurate information is therefore needed based on the official lists notified by the state and Union governments in accordance with the Constitution.“In order to ensure social justice for all sections of society, this Assembly unanimously resolves to urge the union government to collect the caste details of Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities during the second phase of the 2027 census of India, in the same manner as followed for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.”The resolution was passed after legislators, including members of the AIADMK and PMK, spoke in its support.DMK MLAs were not present during the debate and passage of the resolution after they were evicted from the House following a ruckus. Despite their absence, the resolution was passed unanimously.
Article Summary: The Tamil Nadu Assembly has passed a resolution asking the Centre to use only officially recognised caste names while collecting data on Other Backward Classes. Article Title: DMK MLAs bundled out as row over Vijay’s remarks rocks Tamil Nadu assembly

CHENNAI: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday after a stormy confrontation over chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks on late chief minister M Karunanidhi, former Union minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission and ED dossiers relating to cases pending before courts.The dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks, prompting DMK members to raise slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats despite repeated appeals, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.The confrontation began during Zero Hour when DMK whip E V Velu raised objections to Vijay’s remarks made during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department on Monday. Velu accused the CM of making baseless allegations and referring to pending cases, saying this went against the traditions of the House.Referring to the Sarkaria Commission, Velu said late chief minister M G Ramachandran was the principal complainant but later told the commission that he had “no idea whatsoever” about the complaint and that it had been drafted by a party functionary, Kannan from Salem. “At the conclusion, Sarkaria made it clear that there was no prima facie case in all the 28 allegations.Therefore, there was no provision for filing any case,” Velu said.He referred to DK leader K Veeramani and Left leaders being booked under MISA, like DMK leader M K Stalin, and said Vijay’s remarks had demeaned their democratic struggle.Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar defended the CM, saying Vijay had referred to the Sarkaria Commission report and other publicly available documents as part of his fight against corruption. They accused the DMK of being the “root of corruption.”Former minister Govi Chezhiaan then posed three questions to the treasury benches: whether the CM could cite ED dossiers as evidence when the cases were pending before courts? whether the Sarkaria Commission could be selectively used for political gains when it had not found anyone guilty of corruption? and why Vijay had chosen to refer to late leaders such as Murasoli Maran?With no response forthcoming from either the treasury benches or the speaker, DMK intensified its protest.The situation turned chaotic after speaker Prabhakar ruled that there was “no need to expunge the CM’s remarks”. He said Vijay had merely referred to the Sarkaria Commission, whose findings had been discussed in the House earlier, and that the CM’s speech was within the rules of the assembly.The ruling triggered a fresh round of protests, with DMK MLAs raising slogans and sitting in the well, keeping the moments tense for nearly 45 minutes, starting from 9.31am and ending at about 10.11am. In between, the speaker also cautioned minister Aadhav Arjuna for his remarks that they would also match the opposition.The speaker repeatedly asked the members to return to their seats and offered to allow Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. But the DMK members refused to relent.“I will not reverse my ruling,” Prabhakar asserted before directing marshals to remove the protesting MLAs. He cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the Chair.Marshals entered the House at about 10.08am and physically removed several MLAs who refused to leave the well, including Kutty alias A Sudhakar of Valparai, Durai Chandrasekaran of Thiruvaiyaru and Vasantham Karthikeyan of Rishivandiyam.Later in the day, Chezhiaan moved a privilege motion against Vijay, accusing the CM of making “baseless allegations” and citing reports connected to cases pending before courts during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department.
Article Summary: Dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks. DMK members raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.

Article Title: 'Attack on one is attack on all': Pakistan warns Houthis, invokes Mecca defence pact
Article Text:
Pakistan warns Houthis that its defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Turkey

Pakistan warned Tuesday that its newly formed defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could be activated if the conflict in Yemen spills into Saudi territory, saying there should be “no ambiguity” that an attack on any one of the three members would be treated as an attack on all.Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif said the agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Makkah last month was defensive in nature and required the three countries to respond if any member came under unprovoked aggression.“There should be no ambiguity; there is no need for any clarity that this is a joint defence agreement,” Asif said in an interview with Geo TV. He added that Pakistan was “bound by the terms and conditions of this pact” and would honour its commitments to Saudi Arabia if required.His comments came hours after Iran-aligned Houthi forces launched a wave of missile and drone attacks on southern Saudi Arabia, targeting cities as well as economic and energy infrastructure. At least 73 civilians were injured, according to the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen.Asif stressed that the alliance did not give its members a mandate to launch offensive operations against another country on their own initiative.“This is not an aggressive agreement under which the three countries would, on their own initiative, attack another country. But if there is any aggression against one member state, all three member states will respond,” he said.The minister said he was not aware of any contact between Islamabad and Riyadh following the latest Houthi attacks. He also expressed hope that tensions would ease, while warning the Houthis against extending the Yemen conflict into Saudi Arabia.“If they try to export them, the clauses of this agreement to counter aggression will become operative,” Asif said.Pakistan prime minister Shehbaz Sharif separately condemned the Houthi attacks, describing them as “cowardly” and saying they threatened civilian lives as well as regional peace and security. He said Pakistan stood in “unwavering” solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed support for the kingdom's sovereignty, security and territorial integrity.The Saudi-led coalition said the attacks had temporarily disrupted operations at some targeted sites, while specialised teams worked to contain fires and secure the facilities. Riyadh also warned against continued attacks on civilians and commercial shipping.The Houthis said the attacks were retaliation for recent Saudi airstrikes on areas of northwestern Yemen under their control. The group had also accused Saudi Arabia of bombing a prison in Al Hazm on Monday, killing at least 11 people.Asif described the Houthis as “non-state actors” and said sympathy for Iran's position in its ongoing conflict with the United States existed across parts of the Muslim world, including Yemen. But he cautioned against allowing those sentiments to widen the conflict.He also said the Mecca alliance could act as a deterrent without necessarily requiring a military response to every attack.“We don't need to respond to a brick with a stone,” Asif said, arguing that the combined military capabilities of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye should themselves serve as a deterrent.
Article Summary: Pakistan warns Houthis that its defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Turkey could be activated if the conflict in Yemen spills into Saudi territory. Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif said the agreement was defensive in nature and required the three countries to respond if any member came under unprovoked aggression.

Article Title: 'Information sharing is through intelligence channels': Israel denies report UAE leader warned Netanyahu days before Oct 7 attack
Article Text:
Was Netanyahu warned in advance about Hamas attack?

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s office has rejected reports that he was warned in advance about the October 2023, Hamas attacks by UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed.In a post on X, the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office said any exchange of relevant information took place only through intelligence channels between the two countries.“The press reports are false. No warning was given to the Prime Minister by the United Arab Emirates before October 7. If there was any relevant information, it was passed through intelligence channels between the two countries,” it posted.According to a new investigative report published by Israeli newspaper Haaretz, Mohammed bin Zayed had warned Netanyahu that Hamas’ then-leader Yahya Sinwar was preparing a “major attack” on Israel.Netanyahu, however, did not share the warning with Israel’s senior security leadership.Around 10 days after their reported conversation, Hamas launched its attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.The Haaretz report is based on the new book "Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment." It claimed that Mohammed bin Zayed spoke to Netanyahu for 45 minutes from Abu Dhabi.Bin Zayed also reportedly urged Netanyahu to address broader sources of instability, including Gaza’s economic situation and rising tensions in the West Bank.According to a UAE presidential advisor interviewed for the book, bin Zayed was “surprised” by Netanyahu’s response, as the Israeli prime minister did not appear “alarmed”.“He (Netanyahu) said that he believed Hamas was preparing to act in the West Bank and assured him that Israel was ready to respond to any scenario,” the report quoted the adviser as saying.The Emirati leader later discussed the warning with then-CIA Director William J Burns. Bin Zayed reportedly expressed concern that “something there is about to explode” and said Netanyahu had instead focused on the West Bank.Notwithstanding the clarification, the report is likely to pile further pressure on Netanyahu, who has repeatedly been accused of ignoring warning signs in the days leading up to the Hamas attack.The claims are also significant as they come ahead of the Israeli Knesset elections, scheduled for October 27, with Netanyahu seeking a seventh term in office.
Article Summary: UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed reportedly warned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Hamas was preparing a major attack. Israeli PM's office says any exchange of relevant information took place only through intelligence channels between the two countries. Report likely to pile further pressure on Netanyahu, who has repeatedly been accused of ignoring warning signs in the days leading up to the Hamas attack.

Article Title: Toxic air after 9/11: Mamdani releases documents showing how New Yorkers were misled
Article Text:
New York City Mayor Mamdani attends press conference on releasing records on Sept. 11 attacks, in New York (Photo: Reuters)

Days before the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, New York City has reportedly published a number of previously withheld records suggesting officials misled the public about dangerous air quality in the aftermath of the atrocity.At a press conference on Tuesday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled some 170,000 pages relating to health concerns following the collapse of the Twin Towers, Al Jazeera reported.Mamdani said the release would finally bring "accountability" that New Yorkers had long been denied, arguing that "people got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air."Among the papers is the “Harding Memo”, which was sent in October 2001 to then-deputy mayor Robert Harding, which anticipated thousands of lawsuits over "toxic exposure" and set out ways the city might limit its liability.According to the BBC, the memo warned the city could face as many as 35,000 legal claims, partly because health advisories had prompted people to return to the area too soon, risking "toxic exposure or emotional harm."A separate 2002 memo showed officials feared criticism from Congressman Jerry Nadler over asbestos levels could cause a public relations crisis. The BBC reported that this memo, attributed to adviser Ester Fuchs, referenced testimony from the city's health chief claiming no elevated indoor asbestos, even though dust samples showed low levels of the carcinogen.Residents were reportedly told to clean debris with "wet mops and rags," despite guidance that asbestos should only be handled by licensed professionals.Tuesday’s document release also resolves a litigation brought by advocacy group 9/11 Health Watch. The group's director, Benjamin Chevat, said four mayoral administrations had withheld the truth for 25 years while insisting the air was "safe and acceptable".Comedian and long-time advocate Jon Stewart, who appeared alongside Mamdani, said the disclosure was essential even though it could not change past outcomes.According to reports, employees and residents were allowed to return to nearby buildings within weeks of the collapse, as thousands of police officers, construction workers, and firefighters worked in the soot, often reportedly without proper protection.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled 170,000 pages relating to health concerns following the collapse of the Twin Towers. Memo warned city could face as many as 35,000 legal claims, partly because health advisories had prompted people to return to the area too soon.

Article Title: Hurricane Lowell leaves at least one dead, knocks out power in Kauai County
Article Text:
A large wave crashes on the shore caused by Hurricane Lowell on Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026 on the westside of Oʻahu, Hi. (Photo: AP)

This satellite image provided by NOAA shows Hurricane Lowell near Hawaii on September 8, 2026. (Photo: NOAA via AP)

Flights cancelled as shelters house more than 300

Damage caused by Hurricane Lowell is seen on Sept. 8, 2026 in Poʻipū on Kauaʻi's south shore, in Hawaii. (Photo: AP)

650 Kauai residences under voluntary evacuation advisories

This photo taken with a smartphone Damage caused by Hurricane Lowell is seen on Sept. 8, 2026 in Poʻipū on Kauaʻi's south shore, in Hawaii. (Photo: AP)

This photo taken by a smartphone, Damage caused by Hurricane Lowell is seen on Sept. 8, 2026 in Poʻipū on Kauaʻi's south shore, in Hawaii. (Photo: AP)

Lowell passes less than 50 miles from Niihau

Five storms already match typical Central Pacific season

A work crew helps to clean up after damage caused by Hurricane Lowell on Sept. 8, 2026 on the westside of Oʻahu, Hi. (Photo: AP)

At least one person died on Oahu after Hurricane Lowell swept past Hawaii, while wind gusts above 80mph knocked out power to around 90% of homes and businesses in Kauai County as the state began cleaning up Tuesday, according to PowerOutage.com.The death occurred after a tree fell on a tent occupied by a homeless man, Hawaii governor Josh Green said. Kauai County officials also reported storm-related injuries but did not say how many people were hurt or describe their injuries.The county's power provider had not given an estimated restoration time and warned that some outages could be prolonged.Green said Lowell had likely caused damage worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Homes and other structures in Kauai County were damaged by wind and storm surge.All flights at Lihue Airport, Kauai's primary airport, were cancelled Monday afternoon. Hawaii's Department of Transportation said the airport would reopen when it was safe to do so. More than 300 people and dozens of pets were in Kauai County emergency shelters Tuesday morning.State and county offices and public schools were closed Tuesday in Kauai County and on Oahu.Kauai Community College was also closed as cleanup and damage assessments continued.More than 300 National Guard members were deployed across Hawaii. Transportation crews were helping deal with mudslides and storm damage to roads, while other crews were working to restore electricity at hospitals. “There are currently downed power lines, downed trees, debris all over Kauai, so we are really urging folks to stay in place,” Alan Clinton, situation unit leader with Kauai County, said.About 650 residences on Kauai's south and west shores were placed under voluntary evacuation advisories because of the storm-surge threat. Dozens of guests at a hotel in Kapa'a were moved to shelters Monday. Green said waves driven ashore by Lowell “damaged a lot of the area right around the shoreline”.The effects extended beyond Kauai. More than 30,000 customers lost power on Oahu during the storm as tropical-storm-force wind gusts hit the island. High surf also reached a handful of ground-floor units at a condominium in western Oahu.In Maui, coastal flooding closed roads in South Maui and parts of Maui Nui. Maui County reported debris on roads, damage to transport infrastructure and park and service closures.Lowell's centre passed less than 50 miles from Niihau in Kauai County while the hurricane was a Category 2 system. It was the strongest hurricane to affect Hawaii's main islands since Category 4 Hurricane Iniki in 1992.It was forecast to weaken to a tropical storm as it moved farther north from Hawaii. Its strongest winds had already subsided, although forecasters expected more rainfall across areas soaked by the storm.More than a foot of rain had fallen at higher elevations on Kauai. Oahu's Koolau mountains received between 5 and 9 inches, while most other areas recorded between 1 and 3 inches.Forecasters expected surf conditions to improve as Tuesday progressed. A high surf warning remained in effect through Tuesday afternoon for south-facing shores of Kauai County, Oahu County, Maui County and the Big Island.The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has forecast as many as 13 named storms in the Central Pacific this season, compared with about five in a typical year.Five named storms, including Lowell, have already formed in or moved into the region. Two other tropical systems had threatened Hawaii over the previous three weeks.El Nino is contributing to the increased storm potential. Warmer waters in the Central Pacific and weaker upper-level winds create more favourable conditions for tropical systems, while ocean temperatures are also rising over the longer term because of climate change.With Lowell moving farther north, crews were restoring power, dealing with damaged roads and assessing the storm's impact across the affected islands. “We’re doing what we can to recover, but this was a very serious storm,” Green said.
Article Summary: Lowell's centre passed less than 50 miles from Niihau in Kauai County while the hurricane was a Category 2 system. It was the strongest hurricane to affect Hawaii's main islands since Category 4 Hurricane Iniki in 1992. More than 30,000 customers lost power on Oahu during the storm.

Article Title: ‘Can’t live here anymore’: Collapse sends Satya Niketan students packing
Article Text:
Several young residents are packing up their rooms, calling parents and scouting for accommodation elsewhere





NEW DELHI: Suitcases, backpacks and bulging bags are now a common sight in the narrow lanes of Satya Niketan. Two days after a building collapsed in the student neighbourhood, several young residents are packing up their rooms, calling parents and scouting for accommodation elsewhere, as anxiety over the safety of surrounding structures refuses to ease.On Tuesday, Shakib was among those helping a relative empty her room in a building adjacent to the one that collapsed. “She was in the building next door when the incident happened. We reached here within two hours of the incident and her hands were shaking. That is when we decided that she won’t able to live here anymore,” he said. “Now, we are packing everything and taking her to our home in Malviya Nagar.” Some others are taking shelter in colleges at night.Students said one building next to the collapsed structure was being vacated for demolition on priority and several others had been identified as ‘unsafe’. The prospect of further demolition has added to the unease, with residents questioning the condition of other old buildings in the area, many of which, they alleged, have poor ventilation, dangerous staircases and inadequate fire safety provisions.For many, however, moving out is easier said than done. Students said those arriving in Delhi from other states often have little knowledge of its neighbourhoods or the condition of buildings.Their choice of accommodation, therefore, frequently comes down to two considerations -- proximity to college and rent.Rahul, a third-year student of Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, has lived in the same flat since he came to Delhi University. His parents in Dehradun now want him to shift, but affordability remains a concern. “I’m paying Rs 8,000, which is on the lower side. But there is no ventilation or AC,” he said. “If I get something affordable in a better place, like a 1BHK that I can share with my friend and which comes within my budget, I’ll move immediately. ”Fiza, a second-year Jesus & Mary College student whose parents live in Kanpur, stays just metres from the collapse site. “I heard a loud sound that day. When I came out, there was a crowd and a huge pile of debris,” she said. Her parents, she added, may soon come to Delhi and ask her to move out.Some students claimed PG signboards had been removed from a few properties by their owners after the collapse as they feared they will come under the scanner.The collapse has also revived memories of the 2024 Rau’s IAS Study Circle tragedy, where three aspirants drowned in a flooded basement, prompting a crackdown on coaching centres operating from basements. “After that, they closed down libraries in basements. However, now everything is back to normal. They don’t learn,” a student said.The disruption has spilled beyond PGs. On Tuesday, Ramesh, who runs an electrical store nearby, was hurriedly packing his stock into large sacks to move it to his home in Sagarpur. “When the adjoining building is demolished, the debris could reach my shop, so I’m taking everything home,” he said. “My earnings will take a hit, and I don’t know for how long.”In the immediate aftermath of the collapse, some students said mobile connectivity was disrupted due to jammers and they had to walk nearly 500 metres to send messages, photographs and videos to their families. They said connectivity has since been restored.However, Delhi Police Tuesday rejected claims that mobile phone jammers had been deployed at the rescue site, saying networks are fully operational and rescue agencies were communicating through mobile phones without any disruption. In a post on X, police termed the claims “completely false”, saying personnel of Delhi Police, National Disaster Response Force and fire department were coordinating seamlessly through mobile communication.Meanwhile, amid the anxiety, student volunteers have stepped in to help, distributing food and essential supplies to rescue personnel, evacuating students and others at the site.
Article Summary: Suitcases, backpacks and bulging bags are now a common sight in Satya Niketan. Several young residents are packing up their rooms, calling parents and scouting for accommodation elsewhere. Students said one building next to the collapsed structure was being vacated for demolition on priority.

Article Title: Kanpur Murder: Kanpur man beaten to death for objecting to urinating on road; CCTV captures assault
Article Text:
A man died after being assaulted for objecting to public urination.





KANPUR: A 47-year-old man died at a private hospital late Monday, two days after he was allegedly beaten with bricks and stones by four drunken youths for objecting to one of them urinating on the roadside near Om Chauraha in Kakadeo.Police identified the deceased as Amit Kumar, who was returning from his shop in Naveen Nagar at around 11pm on Saturday when he came across four youths drinking near Om Chauraha.According to police, one of the youths allegedly began urinating on the roadside. When Kumar objected, the youth started abusing him, following which the four allegedly surrounded and assaulted him.The youths allegedly repeatedly struck Kumar on the head with bricks and stones, leaving him seriously injured. CCTV footage from the area reportedly captured the assault, with passersby seen trying to rescue Kumar before the attackers fled.Police reached the spot after receiving information and rushed Kumar to a hospital. His family later shifted him to a private hospital, from where he was referred to another facility as his condition worsened. He died late Monday night.Family members gathered at the post-mortem house and demanded the immediate arrest of the four accused.They also alleged police negligence, claiming that no arrests had been made despite CCTV footage of the incident being available.Deputy commissioner of police (Central) Atul Srivastava said Kumar was initially brought to hospital in an injured condition on September 5, with the injuries reported as resulting from an accident. After his death, police examined CCTV footage and carried out local inquiries, which revealed that Kumar had allegedly been assaulted following an altercation.A case has been registered at Kakadeo police station under relevant sections, and four police teams have been formed to trace the accused. Police said efforts were underway to arrest them.
Article Summary: Amit Kumar, 47, died at a private hospital late Monday. He was allegedly beaten with bricks and stones by four drunken youths. The youths allegedly attacked him for objecting to one of them urinating on the roadside. CCTV footage from the area reportedly captured the assault.

Article Title: Beards, blazer, campus protest: Dress code sparks stir in Bengaluru
Article Text:
Students of Indian Academy Degree College staged a protest in Hennur Cross Monday over dress code row





BENGALURU: A college dress code became the unlikely trigger for a student protest in the city Monday, after a group of students of Indian Academy Degree College alleged they were asked to leave the campus for not wearing the prescribed uniform and for having beards.A group of students of the college, in Hennur Cross, alleged that the management asked them to come in uniform and be clean-shaven and get haircuts.When they refused, the authorities allegedly asked them to leave the campus. As the number of students sent off campus increased, they soon united and turned it into a demonstration.As the crowd began to build up on the main road, police also stepped in, fearing traffic disruption.“Monday afternoon, we received a message that some students had come to the road and were protesting. Worried they might block the road, we arrived at the spot. The issue was that many students were not wearing the regular uniform. They had beards, some untrimmed, some with cut lines. We had a discussion and asked them to wear uniform and come dressed decently,” said a police officer.However, the college denied that the students were asked to shave off their beards.“The issue was with dress code compliance. Monday is a uniform day when students have to wear a blazer, tie and shirt. Many of them did not come in uniform. The teachers asked them to go change and come. With this, the students went out and formed a crowd. Police also came in and asked the students to follow the college rules,” said principal Bharathi.“We have told them (students) to be well-groomed. We have a dress code which insists on a proper haircut and well-trimmed beard,” she added.Some students took to social media to express their resentment.“Students wanted a simple explanation. Why are these rules compulsory? Why should students have no choice regarding their appearance? And why weren’t students’ concerns heard properly? Students were sent outside the college gate and made to stand on the main road while the situation continued. This raised an even bigger question: why were students protesting about college rules being pushed outside instead of being heard inside?” read one social media post.“Students raising genuine concerns should not automatically be treated as troublemakers. A college is not just a place where students follow instructions. It is a place where students learn to think, question, discuss and speak up.”
Article Summary: A group of students of Indian Academy Degree College staged a protest in Hennur Cross Monday over dress code row. The students alleged that the management asked them to come in uniform and be clean-shaven and get haircuts. When they refused, the authorities allegedly asked the students to leave the campus.

Article Title: Viral video exposes Fortuner owner using button-operated number plate concealer to evade fine; Rs 1.22L in pending challans found
Article Text:
A Pune man was apprehended for using a hidden number plate device





PUNE: An SUV owner dodged prying eyes of CCTV cameras on roads while speeding and skirted challans as he concealed the vehicle’s registration just by pressing a button. The Tathawade man ran out of luck on Tuesday.The Pimpri Chinchwad RTO tracked him down after a video of his Fortuner's auto-hiding number plate purportedly on Pune-Mumbai Expressway went viral on social media. He was fined Rs 4,500 for unauthorised alteration in his vehicle and the amount was collected on Tuesday.Pimpri Chinchwad regional transport officer Sandesh Chavan told TOI, “After the video was circulated, we checked the SUV’s registration number and found that it had been registered with the RTO office here. Checks on the vehicle revealed that a device connected with wires was installed on the registration number plate. The vehicle owner operated it through a button. When the button is pressed, a black shutter comes down and covers the registration number of the SUV. ”A source in the RTO said the vehicle had 55 pending e-challans, amounting to a total of Rs 1.22 lakh. Most of the challans have been slapped on the vehicle owner for speeding.Each time a fine of Rs 2,000 was slapped on him. Chavan said, “We issued the vehicle owner a fresh challan of Rs 4,500 for unauthorised alteration in the vehicle. He has been warned against repeating the offence and advised to clear all the pending fines without delay. ”He said, “The vehicle owner has been called to the RTO this week again with his vehicle. We will thoroughly check all his vehicle documents again. This is a serious case and we want to set an example so that no one tries the same trick.”Dealers selling automobile spare parts said number plate hiders were easily available on different e-commerce websites for as low as Rs 350 to Rs 400. “We don’t keep it as it is illegal. But some vehicle owners order number plate hiders and a few spare parts shops install the same. Some shops even sell it secretly,” a dealer said,requesting anonymity.
Article Summary: The Pimpri Chinchwad RTO tracked him down after a video of his Fortuner's auto- hiding number plate purportedly on Pune-Mumbai Expressway went viral on social media. When the button is pressed, a black shutter comes down and covers the registration number of the SUV.

Article Title: Sharia courts have no legal authority to issue divorce decrees: Chhattisgarh HC
Article Text:
In a significant ruling, the Chhattisgarh High Court clarified that religious institutions lack the authority to intervene in civil issues.





RAIPUR: The Chhattisgarh HC has held that self-styled Sharia courts or religious bodies possess no statutory authority to adjudicate civil or matrimonial disputes or alter the legal rights and marital status of citizens.Citing Supreme Court precedents, the bench stated that while religious opinion may guide personal faith, no private institution can assume the authority of a legally established court.The court Monday ruled that decisions or fatwas issued by such informal forums carry no legal weight and cannot be enforced through coercive means.A single bench of Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad passed the order while partially allowing a writ petition filed by a Muslim woman, a resident of Raipur. The petitioner had challenged an order dated Jan 18, 2022, issued by the 'Idara-e-Sharia Islami court' in Raipur, which purported to declare her marriage dissolved after her husband, Mohd Abid Khan, pronounced triple talaq.The petitioner contended that private entities cannot assume judicial powers vested in courts established under the Constitution. She submitted that despite lodging complaints of harassment and setting the law in motion, the religious body issued a declaration affecting her marital status without giving her a chance to be heard.The state govt submitted that the Indian constitutional framework does not recognise any parallel judicial system based on religion. It argued that informal bodies styling themselves as Sharia courts or Darul Qaza (Islamic arbitration and counselling centre) lack statutory recognition and function at best as informal conciliation cells.Justice Prasad declared the order issued by the 'Idara-e-Sharia Islami court'' without legal authority and held that the religious body holds no jurisdiction to pass binding adjudications on matrimonial rights.The HC refrained from adjudicating on the constitutional validity of Talaq-e-Hasan, noting that the larger issue remains pending before the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: The Chhattisgarh High Court ruled that religious institutions lack the authority to intervene in civil issues. The HC refrained from adjudicating on the constitutional validity of Talaq-e-Hasan, noting that the larger issue remains pending before the Supreme Court.

Article Title: How row over blocking tourist vehicles at Jaipur's Amer Fort ended in guide's murder
Article Text:
A tourist guide (R) died after being stabbed following an argument near Amer Fort. The deceased was attacked after stopping vehicles and arguing with a driver (L).





JAIPUR: A 40-year-old tourist guide died during treatment at Sawai Man Singh Hospital on Tuesday, a day after he was allegedly stabbed following an argument near Amer Fort, triggering protests and a shutdown of shops in the area.The deceased, Manish Soni, a resident of Amer, was allegedly attacked around 9.30am on Monday after an argument with a tourist vehicle driver, identified as Azam.Police said Soni had stopped vehicles from proceeding towards Amer Fort, leading to an altercation with the driver. The argument allegedly escalated, following which Soni was attacked with a knife and suffered serious injuries to his abdomen.Police said an associate of the accused, identified as Nazish, was also allegedly involved in the attack.Soni was rushed to SMS Hospital and admitted to the ICU but succumbed to his injuries on Tuesday morning. Police said severe injuries and excessive blood loss led to his death.Azam has been arrested and is being questioned, while police are continuing their investigation into the case. DCP (North) Karan Sharma said Soni and Azam had also been involved in a scuffle a few days before the stabbing, though Soni had not lodged a formal complaint.News of Soni's death sparked anger among local residents and tourist guides. Shops in Amer's main market were shut as hundreds of people gathered on the streets to protest.The protesters demanded Rs 1 crore compensation for Soni's family, a government job for a family member and strict action against the accused. BJP MLA Balmukund Acharya reached the spot and held talks with the protesters.Additional police forces were deployed in the area to maintain law and order. Following several rounds of discussions, the protesters dispersed after authorities assured the family of all possible financial assistance and a contractual job.The incident had also triggered a road blockade on Monday soon after news of the stabbing spread.
Article Summary: Manish Soni, 40, died during treatment at Sawai Man Singh Hospital on Tuesday. Soni was allegedly stabbed following an argument near Amer Fort. Incident triggered protests and a shutdown of shops in the area. Police said Soni stopped vehicles from proceeding towards Amer Fort, leading to an altercation with the driver.

Article Title: Watch: Thieves steal Lord Ganesha idol from stall in Bengaluru
Article Text:
CCTV footage screenshot of the group stealing Idol





BENGALURU: Residents were left stunned when even a Ganesha idol kept by the roadside for sale for the upcoming Ganesha festival was not spared by thieves.A group of four men arrived in a mini goods vehicle and made off with the idol in the early hours of Tuesday.According to the CCTV footage, the four men arrived around 3.51am. Article Title: Banker runs over 2-year-old, sister escapes by whisker in Gurgaon
Article Text:
CCTV footage showed the car turning into the lane as the sisters sat and played on the road.





GURGAON: A two-year-old girl playing outside her house died after a banker, allegedly speeding through a narrow internal colony road, ran over her while taking a sharp turn in Sector 5 on Monday night. Her four-year-old sister narrowly escaped being hit by the Volkswagen Taigun.The incident took place around 9pm, shortly after Adrija and her elder sister Chhavija had finished dinner and were playing outside their house. CCTV footage showed the car turning into the lane as the sisters sat and played on the road.Driver Nitin Yadav (31), who works with National Australia Bank as an analyst, failed to spot them, police said, and ran both the front and rear wheels over Adrija.Her mother Pooja was talking to another woman a short distance away when the car screeched into the lane. Chhavija managed to move out of its path as it approached.But Adrija suffered injuries to her nose and mouth and was rushed to Manipal Hospital in Palam Vihar, where doctors declared her dead.Nitin, who lives just four houses away in the same lane, stopped after the accident and took the family to hospital in the same car.He was later arrested from his house.The girl’s father, Virendra Tiwari, an IT engineer with Global Logic in Noida, alleged that Nitin was driving rashly and at high speed on the narrow internal road.He also alleged that the circumstances raised questions about whether the act was intentional and sought stringent action against him.“Our lives have been ruined by rash driving. He cannot drive like this on internal roads. He took the turn at such high speed that he did not even see my children. He could have killed both of them. Adrija would have turned two next month. We are in deep shock. I want the stringent punishment for him,” he told TOI.Tiwari, a native of Mahendergarh, said the family had moved into the rented house about a year ago after living elsewhere in the locality.Based on his complaint, a case was registered under sections 281 (rash driving) and 106 (causing death by negligence) of the BNS at Sector 5 police station. A police officer said Nitin was taken into custody around 3.30am from his house.“He earlier worked abroad and has recently shifted to the city,” the officer said.Police said they have initiated inquest proceedings. The child’s body was handed over to the family on Tuesday after an autopsy.
Article Summary: Adrija suffered injuries to her nose and mouth and was rushed to Manipal Hospital in Palam Vihar, where doctors declared her dead. Her four-year-old sister narrowly escaped being hit by the Volkswagen Taigun. CCTV footage showed the car turning into the lane as the sisters sat and played on the road.

Article Title: Delhi calamities: Magisterial probes flag systemic lapses, action mostly taken against junior staff
Article Text:
Clockwise: Saket building collapse, Satya Niketan building collapse, Vivek Vihar fire, Malviya Nagar fire

Series of tragedies





NEW DELHI: Magisterial inquiries into a series of deadly building collapses and fires in Delhi have repeatedly flagged regulatory failures, negligence and lapses by multiple govt agencies.The subsequent actions, however, have largely been directed at junior govt officials and engineers, even in cases where the probes have pointed to failures involving institutional processes, such as licensing, inspection, monitoring and enforcement.The pattern is evident in the case of the May 30 building collapse near Saket Metro station that claimed six lives, five of them young doctors.A magisterial inquiry that followed held Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) “negligent” as it had “failed” to enforce building bylaws, and concluded that the disaster was preventable.It stated that the collapse was primarily caused by unauthorised structural additions, including illegal third and fourth floors, to the building combined with inadequate regulatory enforcement.Despite the inquiry identifying a failure in enforcement, action was limited to the suspension of two MCD staffers: an assistant engineer and a junior engineer.The case illustrates a distinction between the level at which an institutional lapse is identified and the level at which disciplinary action is taken.A similar gap emerged after the blaze at a bed-and-breakfast establishment in Malviya Nagar on June 3, which killed 23 people.A magisterial inquiry found serious irregularities in the licensing, inspection and monitoring of the B&B and identified lapses by at least four authorities — Delhi Police, MCD, Delhi govt’s tourism department and BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.The action against officials so far has, however, been limited to the sacking of a contractual assistant public health inspector and the transfer of the deputy health officer of South Zone to the headquarters.A magisterial probe into the May 3 fire at a four-storey residential building in Vivek Vihar Phase I, which claimed nine lives, identified lapses by MCD, fire services and Electrical Inspectorate, besides pointing to unauthorised overhead cables that hampered rescue operations.The probe found that Bronto Skylift failed to operate at the scene, most likely because cables, wires and banners became entangled in its boom. It also noted that no effective alternative tall-reach equipment was immediately available. However, no action against officials has been reported so far.Last month, chief minister Rekha Gupta said that based on these reports, actions would be taken against senior officials. However, no major step has been taken until now.A day after Sunday’s Satya Niketan building collapse, five MCD South Zone officials, including the deputy commissioner, superintending engineer, executive engineer (building), assistant engineer (building) and junior engineer (building), were suspended, while a magisterial inquiry was ordered.
Article Summary: Magisterial inquiries into a series of deadly building collapses and fires in Delhi have flagged regulatory failures, negligence and lapses by multiple govt agencies. The subsequent actions, however, have largely been directed at junior govt officials and engineers, even in cases where the probes have pointed to failures involving institutional processes.
