Article Title: Bengaluru Green Crisis: At meet with minister, Bengalureans flag lakes, parks and bigger green crisis
Article Text:
Karnataka’s ecology, forest minister Ramalinga Reddy

Turahalli Exploitation

Pollution, Plastics

Elephants At Events

Western Ghats Echo

Helpline Soon





BENGALURU: Coming under attack from citizens and civil society groups over the govt’s several mega projects and policy initiatives that might negatively impact Karnataka’s ecology, forest minister Ramalinga Reddy Tuesday assured them he would intervene in issues directly under the forest department’s purview, while other matters would be taken up at the govt level for consideration.The minister was participating in a day-long public consultation with citizen groups here. While agreeing with several suggestions, the minister said he had been contemplating amendments to multiple acts and rules to strengthen the protection of Karnataka’s flora and fauna.Big takeaways from the no-holds-barred discussions.Days after the CM announced plans to develop tree parks around Bengaluru, citizens urged the minister not to disturb the natural landscape of Turahalli Reserve Forest. Jeevala Trust recalled a similar proposal during the previous BJP govt that was later aborted.“The govt can make use of Turahalli park, spread over 30-35 acres, and upgrade it into a tree park,” said Subrahmanya Kodipadi. Reddy readily agreed with the suggestion.On parcels of green space set aside for Tunnel Road and other infrastructure projects, Reddy said the legislation had now been withdrawn and there was no proposal to bring it back.With concerns mounting over water and air pollution, representatives from ATREE and other NGOs demanded real-time publication of pollution data from BWSSB, apartment-complex sewage treatment plants and other agencies. Reddy said the govt had already directed apartments, BWSSB and KIADB to rectify lapses affecting waterbodies.“Soon, we will review the compliance and initiate action against offenders,” he said, adding the govt would crack down on single-use plastic items.Wildlife activist Suparna Ganguly and PETA representatives urged the minister to enforce a complete ban on the use of elephants at weddings, festivals and other events, particularly by VIPs and govt representatives. The activists suggested that robotic elephants could be used instead. Reddy responded positively to the proposal.Experts shed light on the implementation of Kasturirangan recommendations on eco-sensitive areas in Western Ghats. Madhuri Mandava, co-founder of Paani.Earth platform, urged Reddy not to reject the Centre’s seventh draft notification. The minister said recommendations would be discussed in the legislature next week.Activists and planters from Kodagu called for large-scale planting of bamboo and fruit-bearing saplings inside forest areas to help retain elephants and other primate species within forests and reduce their movement into human settlements.When Reddy proposed setting up a helpline for queries related to forest dept, citizens pointed to several defunct helplines operated and sought a reliable communication channel.“We’ll set up a fully functional helpline in a day or two, with a dedicated workforce deployed throughout the day to attend to the calls and provide people with the status of their complaints, ranging from forest issues to pollution problems,” he said.
Article Summary: Forest minister Ramalinga Reddy was participating in a day-long public consultation with citizen groups. Reddy said he had been contemplating amendments to multiple acts and rules to strengthen the protection of Karnataka’s flora and fauna. The minister said recommendations would be discussed in the legislature next week.

Article Title: Déjà vu at BKC: In 2023 too, army man, a Modi fan, used tampered NSG card to get close to PM, says ex-cop
Article Text:
A retired assistant commissioner recalled a past security incident involving an army man. He had allegedly used a tampered NSG identity card and fake pass. The army man's intention was reportedly to see the Prime Minister as a fan

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe security measures are sufficient for high-profile visits by politicians? Yes, they are adequate No, they need improvement 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: In light of the Khar resident and his security guard, a former serviceman, allegedly trying to enter Jio World Plaza in BKC a day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s visit on Tuesday, a retired assistant commissioner recalled a case he investigated three years ago.On Jan 19, 2023, an army man allegedly used a genuine but tampered NSG identity card and a fake duty pass to get close to PM during his visit to the MMRDA ground in BKC for the inauguration of Metro lines. The retired officer said the army man’s sole intention was to see PM as he was a fan, and not cause any security problem.A chargesheet was filed in April 2023, while the trial is yet to begin. Police filed the chargesheet within 90 days of registering the FIR.The retired police officer, who served with State Intelligence Special Branch in 2024, told TOI on Tuesday that the army man and his wife later attended PM’s 2024 affordable housing inauguration in Navi Mumbai with a valid invitation pass.BKC police registered an FIR on Jan 20, 2023, under the Indian Penal Code. The army man was released on bail the next day by Bandra court. He was on official leave then and visiting his Navi Mumbai home as his wife was expecting a child.When TOI contacted him on Tuesday, the army man asked why the case was being revisited and said details about the alleged fake duty pass should be sought from the BKC police.
Article Summary: A retired assistant commissioner recalled a past security incident involving an army man. He had allegedly used a tampered NSG identity card and fake pass. The army man's intention was reportedly to see the Prime Minister as a fan and not cause any security problem.

Article Title: PM event arrest: CCTV used to track vehicle, nab youth at his Mumbai home
Article Text:
Mumbai police arrested two individuals claiming PMO affiliation at Jio World Plaza.

d





MUMBAI: A day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s event at Jio World Plaza in BKC, the city police on Monday arrested a 24-year-old Khar resident and his private security guard, an ex-Army serviceman, for entering the premises claiming to be associated with Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). A third person accompanying them managed to flee.The arrested persons have been identified as Khar resident Rohan Parikh, a science graduate, and his security guard Dilip Kunde. The third accused, Worli’s Prathamesh Bagul (26), is on the run.According to the remand application submitted to the court, Kunde was carrying a firearm when the mall’s security personnel stopped them from entering.Parikh allegedly then showed his identity card, claiming to be from PMO, following which the three were allowed inside.Parikh’s lawyers submitted that he might himself have been duped into believing that he was working for the Prime Minister’s Office. He told the police that he suspected the email sender could be fake. They said Parikh had told earlier the police that his PMO identity card was genuine and he was working as a scientist on confidential research after being appointed by a senior PMO official whose identity, he claimed, could not be disclosed at this stage.Public prosecutor Kranti Kumbhar opposed the plea, maintaining that the PMO identity card was fake and that investigators needed custody to determine how it was procured and the motive behind it.The security staff subsequently alerted BKC police after senior officers received information about the trio. Police examined the CCTV footage and traced the vehicle used by them. Investigators identified Parikh using the vehicle registration and mobile number details and subsequently went to his Khar residence, where he was arrested. During questioning, Parikh allegedly identified Kunde and Bagul as the two men accompanying him.The matter was subsequently handed over to Crime Intelligence Unit (CIU). Police have invoked provisions relating to impersonation, forgery and use of forged documents, alleging that Parikh used a fabricated PMO identity card to gain entry into the premises.On Tuesday, CIU senior inspector Milind Kaate produced Parikh and Kunde before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate, Mumbai, seeking their police custody. The prosecution sought four days of custody, saying they needed to establish where the alleged fake PMO identity card was obtained, who prepared it and the motive behind the accused allegedly attempting to gain entry into the premises.The court was told that the identity card allegedly shown by Parikh did not mention the designation of the issuing officer. It carried an issue date but no expiry date. Police have seized the card.Police also seized a revolver from Kunde. Police are examining the source and legality of the firearm. A mobile phone has also been seized from the accused. Investigators plan to extract its contents and examine calls, messages and other electronic communications to establish the alleged conspiracy and determine the respective roles of the three men.During preliminary questioning, Kunde allegedly told the police that he had been working as Parikh’s private security guard for around a year and was being paid Rs 1.20 lakh per month. Kunde, who hails from Nashik, is a former Army serviceman.Parikh’s lawyers Anandini Fernandes and Namita Maneshinde told the court that their client had gone to the mall privately to purchase a perfume and denied that he had any connection with Prime Minister’s visit. The defence claimed Parikh had engaged private security from Dec 2025 after allegedly receiving threats from unknown persons.Magistrate D S Khedekar remanded both accused to police custody till Sept 11. In its order, the court noted that the presence of the accused in an area associated with Prime Minister’s programme, coupled with the recovery of a firearm from the guard in the restricted premises, warranted further interrogation.The court observed that the investigation had progressed with the seizure of the identity card and firearm, but custodial interrogation was required to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident.Parikh is reportedly involved in share trading. His uncle, Amal Parikh, is involved in supplying digital chips used in the manufacture of drones.Parikh’s parents and uncle were present in court during the proceedings but declined to speak to the media.Meanwhile, advocate Satish Maneshinde, on behalf of Parikh, issued a statement saying that the allegations concerned a sensitive subject and that a response would be issued after due verification and investigation. He maintained that Parikh’s visit to Jio World Plaza was “totally private”.
Article Summary: Mumbai police arrested two individuals claiming PMO affiliation at Jio World Plaza. A third person accompanying them managed to flee. The arrested persons have been identified as Khar resident Rohan Parikh, a science graduate, and his security guard Dilip Kunde. The third accused, Worli’s Prathamesh Bagul (26), is on the run.

Article Title: MCD conducts safety survey of 1,150 PGs housing 20,000 people in 1 day
Article Text:
Municipal Corporation of Delhi teams visited 1,150 paying guest accommodations across its zones.

Structural audits and their challenges





NEW DELHI: Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has launched a physical safety survey of paying guest (PG) accommodations within its jurisdiction, following a direction of Delhi High Court On Tuesday, MCD teams visited 1,150 PGs across all its 12 zones and found 20,000 people were staying in the facilities. Around 40 of the buildings require minor repairs and six to eight major repair work, sources said. Their owners were advised to do the needful.“Action has been taken, particularly in Laxmi Nagar, Vishwas Nagar, Mukherjee Nagar, Jamia Nagar, Shaheen Bagh, Tilak Nagar, Karam Pura, Karol Bagh, Ramesh Nagar, Mansarovar Garden, Chandni Chowk and Nehru Vihar. We request people to cooperate in the drive,” MCD stated.In an order issued by its additional commissioner Monday, a checklist was provided outlining the factors to be verified during the survey. They include a building’s sanctioned plan, right of way, the number of rooms and floors and whether it has a structural stability certification.It must also be checked whether conversion charges have been paid, a Delhi Fire Services NOC has been obtained, construction has exceeded the permissible limit and, if so, by how much.While the court has ordered MCD to wrap up the survey within one week, it has decided to complete it by Sept 10.“To meet this deadline, we have pooled in staff from all our departments and asked them to check the condition of columns or load-bearing walls of the buildings,” officials said.Parallelly, LG Taranjit Singh Sandhu and CM Rekha Gupta Monday directed a comprehensive structural audit of the PGs within a week.However, MCD clarified that it does not have an in-house facility for conducting structural audits.“It is important to highlight that the staff is carrying out a physical survey to assess the condition of the PGs and identify buildings that require repairs. Conducting a structural audit is an altogether different exercise. It is time-consuming and has to be carried out by structural experts. Non-destructive testing (NDT) methods used during a structural audit evaluate concrete and steel strength, locate internal flaws and assess corrosion without damaging the building. In Delhi, where 70% to 80% of the buildings are constructed illegally, with no drawings or sanctioned plans, conducting such audits is difficult,” MCD officials said.Experts raised doubts over the completion of the physical safety survey in a week, let alone three days. Aditya Sharma, a structural engineer empanelled with MCD, said, “Conducting a comprehensive survey or visiting all PGs is impossible in three days. Also, unless a thorough inspection or audit is conducted to check the actual condition of such public buildings, incidents like building collapses cannot be averted. In the case of Satya Niketan, the building could have fallen due to structural inadequacy, seepage or sudden alterations to the existing structure. Unless these factors are checked, there is no point in conducting a building survey.”Before every monsoon, the corporation conducts a survey of dangerous buildings, but identifies barely 40 to 50 dangerous ones, Sharma said, adding, “The survey barely helps in minimising building collapses during monsoon. Hope this exercise doesn’t turn that way.”An MCD official said covering the PGs in a short span of time won’t be difficult since most of them are located in select areas close to colleges and universities in Delhi.“The PGs are mostly concentrated in Munirka, Katwaria Sarai, Mukherjee Nagar and other areas close to Delhi University colleges. Also, Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1975 gives MCD staff the power to inspect, repair or demolish structures considered dangerous or ruinous,” the official said.Unlike some other municipal laws, this Act does not specifically mandate routine structural audits of all ageing private buildings, another official said.“Therefore, MCD and the Delhi govt are reportedly working on a stricter policy for periodic structural audits and safety certifications, particularly for older buildings used for public activities,” the official said.In Dec 2023, in response to a PIL, the high court had directed Delhi govt to conduct a comprehensive structural audit of public buildings.
Article Summary: MCD teams visited 1,150 PGs across all its 12 zones and found 20,000 people were staying in the facilities. Around 40 of the buildings require minor repairs and six to eight major repair work, sources said. MCD clarified that it does not have an in-house facility for conducting structural audits.

Article Title: MCD begins demolition of building next to collapsed Satya Niketan PG that killed 7
Article Text:
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi began demolishing a dangerous building adjoining a recent collapse site.





NEW DELHI: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi on Tuesday began the controlled demolition of a building adjoining the structure that collapsed in south Delhi's Satya Niketan on September 6, killing at least seven people and injuring five.An MCD official said the adjoining building had been declared dangerous and the demolition exercise was stopped in the evening. Work will resume on Wednesday morning, the official added.The building had housed a girls' paying guest accommodation and was evacuated after the neighbouring five-storey structure collapsed on Sunday.The MCD had issued an order on the day of the collapse directing the owner or occupier of property No. 13 in Satya Niketan to demolish the structure, citing the danger it posed to residents and neighbouring buildings.Officials had earlier said that the students staying in the building had already vacated it and were returning only to collect their belongings before the demolition.Meanwhile, concerns over unsafe and tilting buildings have also emerged in north Delhi's Nehru Vihar, where residents alleged that a building had tilted several times over nearly a decade because of a faulty sewer line.According to a resident, the structure was demolished and rebuilt once, but developed the same problem again within a few years. The building, which is less than eight years old, was most recently reconstructed around three years ago.Residents alleged that repeated complaints to civic agencies had gone unheard and claimed that poor maintenance by authorities, including the Delhi Jal Board and the MCD, had contributed to the problem.One resident alleged that at least 400 dwellings in the nearby F Block of Gandhi Vihar were tilting in one direction or another. The Delhi Jal Board and the MCD did not immediately respond to the allegations.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: The building had housed a girls' paying guest accommodation and was evacuated after the neighbouring five-storey structure collapsed on Sunday. The MCD had issued an order on the day of the collapse directing the owner or occupier of property No. 13 in Satya Niketan to demolish the structure.

Article Title: Russian dies by suicide at rented room in Goa
Article Text:
Deceased identified as 27-year-old Russian, Pavel Lenskii. (Representative Image)





PANAJI: A 27-year-old Russian, Pavel Lenskii, was dead by suicide in his rented apartment at Bhatir Waddo in Morjim on Monday.His friend Roman Raibinkin, also a Russian, told police that Lenskii had been depressed for the past few days after losing his job and was facing financial difficulties.Police said Raibinkin last spoke to Lenskii on Monday morning when they had breakfast together. After breakfast, Raibinkin went to his room. Around 1pm he found Lenskii’s bedroom door open and discovered his body.Police are awaiting the postmortem report and have so far ruled out foul play.
Article Summary: 27-year-old Russian, Pavel Lenskii, was dead by suicide in his rented apartment at Bhatir Waddo in Morjim on Monday. His friend Roman Raibinkin, also a Russian, told police that he had been depressed for the past few days after losing his job.
